newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Ariane rocket launch delayed.
newsitem.headline: Ariane rocket launch delayed.

text.p: A technical problem aboard Western Europe's 95th Ariane rocket has delayed its scheduled April 11 launch, space officials said on Friday.

"During the Flight 95 preparation campaign in Kourou, French Guiana, a slight anomaly was detected while clamping the Thaicom 3 satellite to its adapter on the Ariane launcher. According to its strict quality control policy, Arianespace has therefore decided to postpone the launch," the Paris-based Arianespace company said in a statement.
"Additional technical checks were immediately initiated and Arianespace will announce a new tentative launch date early next week," it said.
The Ariane-4 rocket is scheduled to launch the THAICOM 3 satellite for Thailand and the BSAT-1 direct broadcast satellite for Japan
The Ariane rocket series is launched from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
Arianespace leads the commercial satellite launch market and has successfully placed into orbit 18 heavy satellites since January 1996 aboard 12 Ariane rockets.
The maiden launch of the new Ariane-5 rocked ended in disaster last June when it had to be blown up shortly after take-off. A new flight is scheduled for September.
Arianespace said its launch backlog for Ariane-4 is 41 satellites worth an estimated $3.5 billion.
